name: Under Armour Inc

events.source: Plank, Q3 FY2026 call 2026-02-06, document_id 188820 ('coming back in the CEO chair in April 2024'); 8-K not in queried window

next_event.source: Lexical 'investor day' search over FY2026 and FY2027 UAA corpus returned only IR website references; no Investor Day or framework update promised. Restructuring plan to be substantially complete by 2026-12-31 (8-K 0001336917-26-000108).

margin_framing.metric_basis_note: Only numeric framing is the one-year FY2027 guide (UA fiscal year ends March 31, so Baba FY2027 = UA fiscal 2027): gross margin +220 to 270 bps, of which about 150 bps is a one-off IEEPA tariff refund, and adjusted operating income of $140M to $160M (a dollar figure, not a margin). No multi-year margin level or annual rate has been stated by Plank or Taleghani. The old 'low double-digit operating margin' long-term objective dates from 2019 to 2021 under prior plans and has not been repeated in FY2026 or FY2027 calls.

statements.quote: For gross margin, we expect expansion of approximately 220 basis points-270 basis points versus last year's gross margin. This outlook assumes a potential refund related to IEEPA tariffs expensed through the P&L in fiscal 2026. This positive impact is expected to contribute roughly 150 basis points, with most of the benefit recognized in the first quarter.

statements.quote: Putting that together and excluding anticipated transformation expenses and restructuring charges, we expect adjusted operating income for fiscal 2027 to be in the range of $140 million-$160 million.

street.gap_assumption: Baba FY labels equal UA fiscal years (year ending March 31). No margin target exists, so the 'target' is the FY2027 adjusted operating income guide midpoint ($150M) plus consensus FY2027 D&A ($105.8M) over consensus FY2027 revenue ($4,744M) = 5.39% EBITDA margin vs consensus 5.21%, +18 bps. Consensus FY2027 operating income $144.9M sits inside the $140M to $160M guide. FY2026 4.36% is actual; FY2029 consensus 6.49%.
street.source: Baba data_financials consensus (Visible Alpha), summary and fundamentals

evidence_of_progress.note: Order [Q4 fiscal 2026, Q1 fiscal 2027]. Q4 FY2026 2.46% vs 0.29% (Baba actual EBITDA $28.8M on $1,171.2M vs $3.4M on $1,180.6M). Q1 FY2027 7.05% vs 4.71%: adjusted operating income $52M plus D&A $25.4M on revenue $1,097.9M (8-K 0001336917-26-000108) vs Baba actual $53.4M on $1,134.1M. Q1 is flattered by the IEEPA tariff refund (gross margin +590 bps 'primarily due to refunds'); the full-year guide carries about $70M of refund benefit, so underlying progress is much smaller. Revenue guide was cut to a mid-single-digit decline on 2026-08-07.

verdict: Weak GXO match: down 60% with a new external CFO, but the founder CEO has been back 30 months, the only numeric framing is a one-year guide inflated by a tariff refund, and consensus already sits inside it.
open_questions: Will Taleghani publish a multi-year operating margin framework once the restructuring completes at 2026-12-31, and when?
Excluding the roughly $70M IEEPA refund, is FY2027 adjusted operating income growing at all on a mid-single-digit revenue decline?
Does the board refresh of April 2025 signal pressure on Plank if the fiscal 2027 'inflection' does not show up in North America?
